text:
Alexander Kerfoot is the kind of forward you notice in the box score only by his blocked shots. He has 21 of them in 19 games for Nashville, against 14 shots of his own, and plays about 16 minutes a night with 6 points (2 goals, 4 assists).

He is not here to create. Over his last ten games he has 0.5 expected goals on his own shots and a single goal, and our numbers had him around 4.3 points over that stretch against the 2 he got. What he does bring is legs (his top speed sits in the 98th percentile on NHL EDGE) and defense: Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.11 fewer expected goals per 60 with him on the ice last season in Utah, 88th percentile, though on a small sample. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 60% of his shots coming off the rush. On a Predators team that has won every game since Oct 31, he is doing the dirty work, and the team is fractionally better at five on five with him than without.
headline: Kerfoot is Nashville's quiet utility forward
